title: Book XII
frozenSupport: Book XII repeatedly separates the ruling faculty from externals, past, future, and other attachments so life can be lived in the present.
Marcus contrasts the weight we give to others' opinions with the lesser value we give our own judgment.
The chapter compresses practice into right action, true speech, purposeful action, and social end.
It repeatedly says to cast away opinion and insists that everything is opinion in the sense relevant to disturbance and assent.
Late sections return to providence, brevity, sameness, and the decisive question of how the ruling faculty makes use of itself.
allowedClaims: presentness in Book XII is about governing assent rather than denying preparation
opinion is the fast lever on disturbance
rightness, truth, and social purpose remain fixed tests to the end
mortality and brevity are used to compress vanity and delay
the final chapter returns everything to the use of the ruling faculty
doNotClaim: that everything is unreal because everything is opinion
that Book XII abandons justice for private calm
that present focus forbids planning or foresight altogether
that Marcus ends in pessimism or meaninglessness
